lesson: A managed assembly is read as its metadata tables plus the assembly row that names it, so the identity a runtime would bind against - name, version, culture, hash algorithm - is reported as the file states it rather than as the filename suggests. Exactly one Module row is not a quirk: the format allows one per file, so a reader finding two is reading something that is not an assembly. The tables are named as well as numbered because the numbers are the format and the names are this reader’s interpretation of them.
